planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in fertile, evenly moist soil; also excellent for fall sowing about six to eight weeks before first frost.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in fertile, evenly moist soil, spacing plants to allow the glossy dark-green leaves and tender white stems to fill out into a compact, slow-bolting head. Black Summer was bred as a heat-tolerant companion to white-stemmed types like Joi Choi, so it can be planted through the warmer parts of the growing season with far less risk of premature flowering. Harvest at 8-10 inches tall for a sweet, crisp bok choy suited to stir-fries, soups, and fresh use.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1 inch deep once soil has warmed well past last frost, since this open-pollinated Japanese heirloom edamame needs consistent summer warmth to fill its pods.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1 inch deep once soil has warmed well past last frost, since this open-pollinated Japanese heirloom edamame needs consistent summer warmth to fill its pods. Plants set heavy clusters of two- to three-bean pods on compact, well-branched bushes and are valued in trials for their reliably smooth, sweet, nutty-flavored beans. Harvest whole pods when plump but still green, then steam or boil briefly in salted water for a classic edamame snack; being non-hybrid, seed can be saved from healthy plants for replanting.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1 inch deep after soil has thoroughly warmed and all frost danger has passed, providing a sturdy trellis for the vigorous climbing vines.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1 inch deep after soil has thoroughly warmed and all frost danger has passed, providing a sturdy trellis for the vigorous climbing vines. This classic Cantonese-type cultivar produces oblong, blunt-ended fruit with a pale-green, gently warty surface that is larger and milder than typical Indian bitter melon types. Harvest fruit while still firm and light green, before the surface begins to yellow, for use in stir-fries, stuffed dishes, and soups where its characteristic bitterness is balanced with garlic, black bean, or egg.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in rich, well-drained soil timed for a fall harvest; thin plants to their full spacing early so uniform heads can develop.

directions: Direct-sow seed 1/4 inch deep in rich, well-drained soil timed for a fall harvest, since this fast-growing hybrid is bred for slow bolting and reliably forms dense, barrel-shaped heads even under variable weather. Thin plants to their full spacing early so uniform, well-wrapped heads can develop without stress cracking. The crisp, mildly sweet leaves are well suited to fresh salads, quick stir-fries, and kimchi, and mature heads store well in a cold, humid location for several weeks.

planting.note: Direct-sow seed thinly and shallowly, about 1/4 inch deep, in fertile soil; also excellent for fall sowing six weeks before first frost.

directions: Direct-sow seed thinly and shallowly, about 1/4 inch deep, in fertile soil, since this miniature pak choi matures in as little as 30 days and can be grown at very tight spacing for dense baby-green production. Its curled, glossy dark-green leaves sit atop short, thick white petioles, giving each plant a compact, rounded form even smaller than standard baby bok choy. Because it thrives across a wide range of temperatures, it can be succession-sown nearly year-round in mild climates for continuous harvests of whole tender plants used raw, steamed, or stir-fried.
